content:
Hey everyone, I recently came across this feature of lean .., which allows us to write foo 1 _ _ _ as foo 1 ..

I was thinking about writing a linter for this feature so mathlib will actually use this.
I want to do this because it will be more readable and be more immune to refactoring changes in the methods used (for example if a typeclass was separated into 2 different typeclasses, we would need to add _ everywhere), which means less work for mathlib maintainers.

So while I am making this linter, I was just curious on any comments on the topic, whether mathlib would benefit from it and any implementation notes.

Oh one thing to note is that _ is not always interchangeable with .., particularly, it creates metavariables from holes that lean cant resolve, which means that we have to check to only replace _ suffixes, nothing of the form foo 1 _ _ _ h.

Furthermore, we need to distinguish between ordinary _ holes and optParam / autoParam holes, which, in my understanding, can override the behaviour, so we need to avoid the linter working on those as well.

What about you first find all occurrences of _ _ in mathlib, then see how many of these can be replaced? I would be happy to merge a PR doing those changes on the basis that it is adopting a syntax that was not available at the time of the code being written

so i havent finished fully making the PR, but in the process of building the linter, I see 13500 instances of this pattern that can be replaced (some edge cases not verified yet), with the most egregious being CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesPullback_symmetry with 9 different holes.
Replace them, open a PR, and run !radar, I guess?

I would argue that this change is potentially harmful, because:

  • .. is sure to be slower to elaborate than _, because Lean has to work out the number of _s.
  • .. can make the proof harder to repair, since the maintainer has to first replace .. with the right number of _s before they can work out which one to pass explicitly.
wouldn't it just be better to use the named arguments

Aditya Menon said:

with the most egregious being CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesPullback_symmetry with 9 different holes.

But how are you replacing those with ..? It doesn't work when there are more function params to consume
(btw that's more than a human, according to Vsauce)

Eric Wieser said:

  • .. can make the proof harder to repair, since the maintainer has to first replace .. with the right number of _s before they can work out which one to pass explicitly.

We can fix this by adding a code-action though, right?

Instead of making 13,500 changes at once, why don't you start with the cases where there are a lot of underscores in a row (significantly more than two). Those are the places where more space/characters can be saved.
For code like foo _ _ _ _ _ _ _ a, a better fix is generally to pass a as a named argument. Mathlib has some cases with many consecutive underscores. Usually, I'd take a PR making such a replacement.

Snir Broshi said:

Aditya Menon said:

with the most egregious being CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesPullback_symmetry with 9 different holes.

But how are you replacing those with ..? It doesn't work when there are more function params to consume
(btw that's more than a human, according to Vsauce)

sorry, I meant FreeAlgebra.lift_unique which has 9 holes, preservesPullback_symmetry actually has 11 holes, but will not work with .. notation because it doesn't follow the suffix rule.
FreeAlgebra.lift_unique only has two holes unless you write it with @.

I do agree that for performance reasons, ones with 2 holes should not be replaced with ellipsis, I am building a setting to toggle how many holes should be flagged, I am thinking 4 or 5 holes for now? this would be roughly 600 and 200 instances found respectively, with further filtering needed.

Eric Wieser said:

FreeAlgebra.lift_unique only has two holes unless you write it with @.

Omg, sorry, I meant Quiver.FreeGroupoid.lift_unique
That only has three, not 9
what

I am trying to quote this line

fapply @Quiver.Symmetrify.lift_unique _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _

perhaps this works:

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/cdc4a098a5e8c3b234f61f1529f752cfb7df8714/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Groupoid/FreeGroupoid.lean#L163-L175

Michael Rothgang said:

For code like foo _ _ _ _ _ _ _ a, a better fix is generally to pass a as a named argument. Mathlib has some cases with many consecutive underscores. Usually, I'd take a PR making such a replacement.

I also do think this is a good idea to lint for in a future PR

Eric Wieser said:

  • .. is sure to be slower to elaborate than _, because Lean has to work out the number of _s.

I'm not sure this is actually true: I think .. always expands to as many _s as possible, and so there should be no significant difference in elaboration speed.

I would imagine that in fact there will be issues where it's not clear how many _s are needed (because some things which you don't expect to unfold to functions, do unfold to functions internally) and so you will get the occasional sporadic instance when it's either a fair bit slower or just fails outright. I agree that 95+% of the time it will make no difference.

Aditya Menon said:

I am trying to quote this line

fapply @Quiver.Symmetrify.lift_unique _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _

This example is needlessly using @ notation to manually specify implicit parameters that are then not specified, it works to just replace it with

fapply Quiver.Symmetrify.lift_unique _ _
Perhaps a more useful linter would look for @foo _ _ _ (> 2 underscores) and say "use named arguments instead"
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/ContMDiff/Basic.lean#L477
in case you're too lazy to count, that's 28 holes

.. doesn't seem to always work as expected, for example in https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/cdc4a098a5e8c3b234f61f1529f752cfb7df8714/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/SnakeLemma.lean#L289 the term SnakeLemma.exact_δ_left (hπ₂ := hπ₂) (hF := hF) (h := h) _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ works fine, as does adding up to two more holes, but replacing the holes with .. doesn't because it seems to be too eager and fill in one more hole than necessary so you get the wrong term, though you could fun _ ↦ SnakeLemma.exact_δ_left (hπ₂ := hπ₂) (hF := hF) (h := h) .. if desired. Not clear it's worth it, but I was just enjoying looking at the cases with the most holes.
#42205 fixes the above example with 28 holes, by the way. We can do better these days :-)
The snake lemma looks like an actual snake
that's why it's called the snake lemma!

Kevin Buzzard said:

I would imagine that in fact there will be issues where it's not clear how many _s are needed (because some things which you don't expect to unfold to functions, do unfold to functions internally) and so you will get the occasional sporadic instance when it's either a fair bit slower or just fails outright.

You are right, I failed to consider that it could take a while for .. to realise that it's done.

Relatedly I have often wished that .. didn't unfold (or maybe only unfold as necessary to fill in at least 1 argument) because I try to use it on something that e.g. returns a Function.Injective and it doesn't work

I thought that the .. ellipsis simply fills in as many arguments as possible, so there should be no slowdown from using it. And as you say, this might be filling in too many arguments if the return type is Function.Injective.

.. will also synthesise CoeFun instances (and, as I mentioned, unfold definitions), and compared to an expression which has the correct number of _s prewritten, in general it has to attempt to do these one more time and fail, to realise that it has as many arguments as possible. Probably it isn't a significant difference in practice though.
Sorry, it seems like the part about synthesising CoeFun is a lie. (So it should make even less of a difference)
Which, I guess, is yet another difference between .. and a bunch of _s

I have almost the entire linter done now, and pretty much all of mathlib has gone down fine, apart from exists_integral_inj_algHom_of_quotient on line 265.

Out of all 8000+ files on mathlib, this particular line is the only error, and I have been really puzzled on what could be different about this particular line

anyway, in a use of the Ostrich algorithm, I believe that for performance reasons the best way to deal with this is simply to modify this particular lemma slightly instead, and hope that the fact this is the only instance means that it is a very rare issue. I put a PR for it here, #42266
Because IsIntegral R has function type (see docs#IsIntegral). I'm very surprised this is the only error you get in Mathlib actually
The PR is now up here

Hi everyone, the PR has been up here, my PR creates warnings, and it seems that the mathlib CI converts build warnings into CI build fails, see here

So I am uncertain what to do, my linter fundamentally makes warnings, and the CI fails all warnings
Either you fix all the warnings, or you find a way to silence them

Well my original plan was not to fix all the warnings, because there are about 431 files that the linter is warning on (intentionally), i expected to make a follow up PR where I fix this in batch, so that the i dont have a massive PR that changes a ton of files.

I expect that if there are a lot of changes, my PR will take forever to be reviewed
Would it make sense for me to put the PR with my linter disabled in the first PR, and then the second PR where i change all the offending files, in that file the linter gets enabled

You could still execute the same plan, but in reverse order: first make some PR(s) that do the fixes, and then after that the actual linter could be merged.

Based on the adaptations, the reviewers can decide whether this linter is a good idea to have in mathlib
